correctness.rationale: The claim is about the ordinary orbit space for the full graph-automorphism group. The given adjacency is the two pentagonal belts with poles of an icosahedron: poles 6 and 7, belts (1,2,3,4,5) and (8,9,10,11,0), with the staggered cross edges. An independently written enumeration recovered all 120 automorphisms, face counts (12,66,140,105), and the elimination of all 55 edge generators of the complex's fundamental group in rounds of 35 and 20. The two vertex-fixing automorphisms generate the full group, so Armstrong's theorem kills the quotient fundamental group. Rank order forces any identification within a closed flag simplex to fix its support pointwise, and the cellular incidences are the alternating flag deletions. Independent exact Smith reductions on the 9,905 flags give orbit cell counts (10,35,49,24), zero successive compositions and boundary Smith ranks (9,26,23) with every nonzero factor a unit. A primitive image in the ambient chain group is also primitive in the kernel, so these ranks and unit factors give only H0 and H3, both Z. Hurewicz and homological Whitehead applied to a representative of a generator give the stated S^3 equivalence.
residual_risks: No homeomorphism, manifold structure, equivariant equivalence or infinite-family claim is established or needed.

value.rationale: The full-symmetry orbit space of a canonical highly symmetric graph complex is a motivated exact object: a prior calculation already isolates its rational sphere homology while leaving integral and homotopy information unresolved. A researcher using this quotient needs to know whether integral torsion or a nontrivial fundamental group survives stabilizers. The exact finite check and fixed-point argument resolve both, not by a mechanical rational-invariant deduction.
residual_risks: Value is for the precise full geometric quotient, not a general result for polyhedral graphs.
